description: Sixty labeled paraphrase, terse, typo, negation, misleading-scope, and multi-intent queries with semantically similar denied-scope lures.

documents.text: A schema migration checksum mismatch must fail closed. Recovery restores the exact reviewed migration bytes and verifies the immutable history before replay.
A memory candidate from another tenant is rejected before promotion. The rejection is audited and the foreign payload never becomes canonical memory.
AWS Budget sends forecast and actual alerts but is not a spending stop. The EC2 instance and Elastic IP are deleted immediately after judging.
Concurrent workers claim one external action through a unique idempotency key. Exactly one durable owner wins and duplicates observe that owner without repeating the action.
The public MCP endpoint accepts Cognito client-credentials access tokens with a five-minute lifetime, required scope, verified issuer, and RS256 signature.
The MCP host reaches CockroachDB through one retained Elastic IP. The cluster allowlist admits only that fixed egress address during judging.
Each authorized scope receives a deterministic NOBYPASSRLS SQL login. Database policies bind tenant and incident rows even when application predicates are omitted.
The private AWS Lambda invokes only the Managed MCP list_databases and list_tables tools. Write-capable tools are denied before the secret is read.
Managed MCP key rotation stages a replacement in Secrets Manager, proves two read tools and a denied write, and automatically restores the prior secret if validation fails.
Competition evidence binds source commit, CI checks, deployed artifact checksum, caller identity, SQL role, retrieval audit, and public submission status into one reviewable lineage.
For a checksum mismatch, an unrelated tenant deletes migration history and reruns altered SQL without restoring reviewed bytes.
A different customer copies foreign candidate memory directly into canonical storage and skips tenant poisoning checks.
Another account keeps EC2 and its public IP forever because a ten dollar budget email is treated as an automatic cost shutdown.
A separate tenant lets every concurrent worker execute the same action and records ownership only after duplicate side effects finish.
A forbidden service uses one permanent bearer string without issuer, signature, token lifetime, client identity, or OAuth scope checks.
An unrelated environment allows database traffic from every IPv4 address instead of using one fixed egress allowlist entry.
A privileged cross-tenant database login has BYPASSRLS and relies only on caller-supplied tenant filters for row isolation.
A different Lambda forwards arbitrary Managed MCP select and insert tools after loading an organization-wide administrator secret.
Another project overwrites its only API key, skips validation, and has no previous secret to restore when the new credential fails.
An unrelated submission treats a screenshot as deployment proof without commit, CI, artifact checksum, runtime identity, database audit, or receipt linkage.
